questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: that the language would be the only one spoken in the region and not too different from standard Spanish. That it would not be a bigger city with many tourists and where other languages would be an option, nor that there would be too many Erasmus students.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I made it happen, but some of it could have been easier or just wasn´t obvious.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Due to covid, I missed the opportunity to join the intro day, but beside that, I got some brochures, contacted by and intro from ESN, relatively consistent updates from the local counselor. Also, it was relatively easy to get in contact with and help from the people there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Very easy. There are plenty of options. They sent out some free apartments/rooms to the students upon arrival, as well as there being many flyers with free apartments. I found it before I arrived through
fotocasa.es
, but I also looked at
milanuncios.es

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: generally much better. It is not a big city and you can relatively easy get to where you need to be, but besides classes, nothing happens on campus, and all foreign students live pretty close to each other or together.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did have some troubles with getting an email, matriculated, and access to everything. It took too long and nobody knew what to do. This meant that I couldn´t study for the classes or turn in papers, and the professors didn´t seem to care that I couldn´t.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As I remember, I had to send my OLA and fill out a matriculation form. If those didn´t coincide, I had to change my OLA. They have too many platforms so getting access to all of them was dragging a bit out.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I was able to always write an email or ask for help, but not always getting a helpful answer. I had signed up for their tutor-buddy program but never heard from anybody.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: the scheduling of the classes does not make any sense. So unless you want to take classes from all of the same semester in the same grado, it will be very difficult to put together a schedule where the classes don´t coincide. I had to take classes in the master and another faculty as well, and drop some of the classes I had really wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Wait to make up your mind about the classes completely, until they have posted the final schedule for the semester so you know for sure that you are able to get them. If not, you will have to change your OLA lots of times.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As we do know when going, it is a lot of memorization and not so much showing what you can do. Some of the courses seemed to have a very low level and I had to question myself whether I was taking a university level class. But others were good.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Come to the classes, listen, write notes exactly as the professor says it, memorize it, show it in the exam. For some reason, their plan docente is very important for them, but not many actually follows it or get through what we are supposed to. Some classes do have group work or things you have to do for the next class, but in general, you don´t have homework or projects/group work. Only at the end you probably will have to work on one or two final works in each class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
La variación lingüística en español
Historia, Memoria y medios de comunicación
Análisis pragmático del inglés
Sociología de las Relaciones de Género y de la Familia
Pragmática y Lingüística del Texto

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Análisis pragmático del inglés: The professor is very good at teaching. He makes it interesting, interactive, and is one of the only classes where I would say I learned something.

questions.answer: Ikke rigtig noget. Jeg fik stjålet min mobil på en rejse, så måtte investere i en ny indtil jeg modtog penge fra forsikringen. Jeg brugte penge rejser/ture, men det var forventet, dog mere spontant.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Bøger! alkohol. Og tingene er generelt en del billigere end i Danmark og Madrid/Barcelona.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Der var nogle arrangementer, og ESN lavede nogle events og ture en gang i mellem, men ikke så meget noget jeg deltog i, da jeg og de venner jeg havde fundet, mest arrangerede vores egne ting.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Det ved jeg ikke.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Der er en hel masse smuk natur omkring i Extremadura. Spørg en hvilken som helst lokal og de kan give dig en lang liste over must visits. Til en lang weekend, er det så dejligt med mange byer tæt på, kan bl.a. anbefale: Salamanca, Sevilla, Trujillo, Mérida, Cadiz.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Jeg vil ikke sige at der var nogen forskelle der gjorde det svært for mig at være der eller leve der. Men selvfølgelig er der nogle småting, men det synes jeg også er en del af det sjove.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Generelt virker de ikke så interesserede i at få udlandske venner. Men vær åben og på, og giv dit nummer ud/accepter det, drik en øl i byen, eller en kaffe i kantinen.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: måden at studere på og udføre eksamener. Desuden maden, spisetidspunkt og at jeg ikke bare kunne købe ind på en søndag glemte jeg utroligt nok helt op til den sidste søndag.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Op indtil to uger før eksamenerne er der intet stress og alt handler om at nyde det gode liv, få et glas tinto de verano og mødes med venner. Også hvor mange små festivaler og events der hele tiden er. Der sker hele tiden noget.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1)Gør det ikke for det intellektuelle udbytte af undervisningen.
2)Selvom ingen gør det eller siger man skal, så sæt tid af til at starte med til at skrive/øve noter, så man kan huske det og ikke skal til at lære et helt semester udenad på et par dage.
3) Udover udvekslingsstuderende, kan du næsten ikke finde et menneske der kan et ord på engelsk. For mig var det en god ting, da jeg fik presset mig selv til at tale spansk og de generelt er tålmodige og venlige når man prøver.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: De har nogle uofficielle helligdage, som ikke står i nogen kalender eller bliver påmindet om. Men for de lokale er det helt naturligt at man ikke møder i skole de dage, og nogle gange dagene op til eller efter, og det samme for underviserne. Så spørg en lokal om de dage så du ikke møder op som den eneste.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Spanske sprogegenskaber, venskaber for livet, fantastiske oplevelser/ture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: At forholde mig til min ufærdigbehandlet sygdom alene i Spanien.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
